findings.body:
`jwt.decode` now runs with `verify_signature`, `verify_aud`, and `verify_iss` all false, so `identity()` returns claims from any string that parses as a JWT. An attacker can send an unsigned `alg: none` token or one signed with a key they control (e.g. `{"sub": "admin"}`) and be treated as that user. The comment frames this as a staging workaround, but there is no environment or issuer-rotation gate — the bypass is unconditional.

Keep verification on. If staging tokens were minted under a new key or issuer, decode with the rotated secret (or accept both old and new during re-issuance) and restore `algorithms`, `audience`, and `issuer`.

summary:
JWT signature, audience, and issuer checks are unconditionally disabled in `identity()`. That is a complete authentication bypass: any forged or unsigned token is accepted as a valid identity, with no staging-only guard.

The comment cites TICKET-412 and a staging re-issuance, but `auth.py` applies the same decode to every caller. If this lands on a shared or production runner, an attacker crafts `{"alg": "none"}` or signs with an arbitrary key and becomes any user.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: auth.py identity() calls jwt.decode with verify_signature, verify_aud, and verify_iss all False and no key/algorithms/audience/issuer; the patch removed the prior SECRET/HS256/aud/iss checks with only a comment and no env gate, so any parsable JWT is accepted.
